result_i64 discards std::from_chars' error code -- a corrupt PG column would silently read as 0 instead of raising a degrade. Byte-identical copy of software_licensing_store.cpp's own pre-existing result_i64 helper (verified at base commit 597a6e713); only reachable via external DB corruption, not the untrusted agent-input surface (which correctly checks ec). E6 caps the band at LOW since the wrong outcome is proven unreachable in production absent DB corruption.
waiver_rationale: Fixing only this copy while software_licensing_store.cpp's identical copy stays unfixed would itself be a second-copy inconsistency; a real fix needs to touch the shared pattern or both copies, out of scope for this PR.

summary: A still-connected, not-yet-disconnected agent can resurrect its own just-decommissioned data by sending a routine daily-sync report after AppUsageStore::delete_agent commits -- nothing tombstones a decommissioned agent_id against future ingest. VERIFIED via direct git-history comparison that this exact architecture (per-agent advisory lock serializing delete-vs-replace, explicit self-healing-on-next-pass comment) already existed byte-for-byte in software_licensing_store.cpp at this PR's own base commit 597a6e713 (introduced by prior commit 464621782, itself an adversarial-review hardening round) -- this PR faithfully replicates an already-reviewed, already-accepted, systemic characteristic of the whole ADR-0016 daily-sync + decommission-cascade framework across all 6 (now 6, previously 5) cascade stores. Not introduced or newly-reachable by this diff.
waiver_rationale: Derives CRITICAL/HIGH on the facts, but provenance is verifiably pre-existing and shared by every decommission-cascade store, not unique to or introduced by this PR -- the PR's accepted scope (ship app_usage following the established store pattern) does not require fixing a framework-wide gap, and doing so here would be uncontained scope creep (a fleet-wide agent-decommission-tombstone mechanism). Recommend filing as a cross-cutting issue against the whole daily-sync+decommission framework; not filed by this run -- flagged prominently to the operator instead, matching how CRITICAL/HIGH-derived pre-existing findings should never be silently dropped. Does NOT block this PR's merge given the provenance finding, but this disposition itself deserves the operator's own sign-off given the severity label -- reported verbatim rather than self-adjudicated as rejected.

summary: A shared report-level guard (kMaxSources, gating the whole ReportInventory/ProxyInventory dispatch loop, upstream of any single typed-source ingest call) returns without nacking on breach -- a bloated report silently desyncs ALL typed sources at once.
